params.prompt:
Create a production sprite-sheet IMAGE for a side-view pixel-art fighting game. Exactly FOUR columns and FOUR rows, exactly SIXTEEN separate complete-character animation cels in a regular 4x4 grid. Read the poses left-to-right then top-to-bottom. No text, numbering, labels, borders or dividing lines. Pure flat vivid magenta #FF00FF background, including every gap; no ground shadow, scenery, gradient or checkerboard. Crisp deliberate pixel clusters, dark clean outlines, restrained highlights, no blur or antialiasing. Same character identity, head size, limb lengths, clothing and camera scale in every cell. Strict right-facing 3/4 fighting view, both eyes visible where anatomically appropriate. Exactly two arms and two legs, all attached, no baked resting arm beneath a moved arm, no duplicate hands. Keep every full silhouette inside its own 256x256 cell with 18 pixels of empty margin. Use the same ground line at y=230 within each cell. Standing head-to-foot height about 168 pixels; keep that anatomical scale for crouches and lying poses rather than enlarging them to fill the cell. Never crop ears, spikes, hands or feet. Preserve gaps between legs. No travelling projectiles, beams, particles, trails, detached props, partner or extra characters: draw BODY performance and established attire only; the game draws effects separately. The supplied original image is the authority for face and identity. Complete its unseen lower body consistently as described. The poses are successive purposeful key drawings, not recolored duplicates.
FIGHTER: Golden Sproto. Use the supplied ORIGINAL reference as the identity authority, not previous rigging or generated bodies. Golden-yellow spiky feline head with pointed ears, one black inner-ear wedge; green heavy eyelids/eye surrounds; white eyes with large black pupils and white highlights; round black nose; broad deep-red curved lips. Yellow throat, red scarf/neck band, black formal jacket, yellow pointed shirt collar, red tie. all exposed body yellow; retain green eye surrounds and red lips rather than recoloring the entire face yellow. Continue formal black clothing, yellow shirt and red tie. Matching black trousers/shoes are a reasonable completion, not visible original facts. Preserve these distinctive details in every frame; do not normalize into a generic mascot. Full-body completion must remain consistent across all 32 frames.
Sheet A contains these exact 16 cels.
ROW1: Intro, four consecutive full-body poses: (1) relaxed guard; (2) first half of this signature introduction: Straighten red tie, roll shoulders and raise a confident guard.; (3) second half of that gesture; (4) settle into the same right-facing fighting guard.
ROW2: Signature special, first four poses: (5) body compresses and gathers strength; (6) full anticipation; (7) first clear contact silhouette; (8) controlled retraction. Performance: Four advancing alternating punches, pronounced coiled windup and full-body finishing cross. Draw the character only, no effects or actual projectile.
ROW3: Same signature special, last four poses: (9) second different contact silhouette using the other shoulder/arm; (10) retraction/coil before finishing; (11) strongest final contact with coherent hips/knees/ankles; (12) balanced planted recovery. These poses are used at actual combat contact times; do not invent extra limbs or multiple bodies to imply speed.
ROW4: Ranged cast, four consecutive poses: (13) prepare; (14) maximum anticipation; (15) release; (16) follow-through returning to guard. Performance: Cheeks inflate, chin draws back, horizontal golden spit release, mouth relaxes. The mouth/hands show release, but DO NOT draw the travelling spit/projectile. Mouth stays attached to face and both arms remain distinct.
Every cell must preserve the original identity exactly. No generic replacement mascot.
